_note: Generated outfits (decision 0008): which garments each outfit image yields, their slots, and the body regions each may sit on. Colours come from the generated texture; each garment's colours (the prompt's, as hex) only settle which garment owns a colour lying where two garments meet. A garment's loosest overrides its slot's cap on how far a fitted garment stands off the body (make_generated_outfit.LOOSEST). A garment's straps (metres) adds shoulder straps that wide (so its edges can be smoothed as much as any). A garment's scoop (metres) cuts a scoop neckline that deep. A garment's band adds a belt or waistband (width in metres, colour) along its top edge. A garment's sleeve_ease (metres) is the least its sleeves stand off the arm. A garment's top (metres above the floor) is as high as it reaches. A garment's flare [metres, over metres] adds ease towards its hem (A-line shorts). A garment's gather (metres) draws its ease in over that stretch above the hem (joggers' cuffs). A garment's ease (metres) is the least it stands off the body (baggy joggers). A garment's edge_blur (metres) overrides how much its edges are smoothed (thin straps need little). A garment's length (metres above the hip joint) is a level hem it stops at, not tucked in (a hip-length jacket). A garment with one_shoulder (left or right) has only that strap. A garment with halter true has its straps rise from the bust to a band round the neck instead of going over the shoulders. A garment with hood true also takes its hood from the scan (garment_tools.extract_hood). An outfit with body masculine was generated on the masculine base and is measured against the body's masculine shape. Tops and bottoms meet at one waist line (garment_tools.WAIST_ABOVE_HIPS) unless a top is tucked (metres above the hip joint its hem stops), or opts out with waist false (swimwear, lingerie, crop tops). A garment's ring adds a level band at its top or bottom edge (width in metres; back band also closes it round the back, as a bra's). A garment's neck (metres) is how far up the neck its collar reaches, and hem (metres below the hip joints) where its legs end. A garment with a skirt is built as one tube from the waist line (garment_tools.build_skirt): its offset, flare (widening only, down to the hem), straight (no widening below the hips), smooth, pleats and pleat_depth, and hem (metres above the floor, where the scan's is unclear), and widest (metres it may stand off the body at the hem: a sheer overlay scans as a tent); a fitted garment with a skirt is a dress, its bodice cut at tucked. A garment's fill lists body regions it covers whatever the scan shows (tights under a skirt; a cream blouse whose highlights read as skin). A garment with one colour has one recolour region unless solid is false. An outfit with legs_hidden (a floor-length gown) aligns its scan with the legs where ours are, moved with the hips: the joints found for hidden legs are guesses, and they dragged the hem in. Each garment's name, tags, lean, contexts, weight, excludes_tags and requires_tags are its catalog entry (update_sidecars.py). A garment's fabric (Tools/Textures/fabrics.py) is what it's made of: its material's surface texture. fabrics lists the other fabrics the same garment can be made in (the generator picks one per item). patternable says whether it can take a print (Tools/Textures/prints.py) on its main fabric. Rule tags: long_legs marks trousers that reach the ankle, which tall boots exclude (both sit the same layer off the skin, so the shafts came through the trouser legs); jeans cut to tuck into boots aren't long_legs.
